findings.reason: a node implementing the deliverable literally blocks the failure-recording path, and the plan's own thesis is that only landed work must be on main, so the refusal must be scoped to a passing promotion.
findings.text: §5 refuses "a plain crew complete on an implementation run whose reviewed head is not an ancestor of the remote primary branch" without conditioning the refusal on a passing gate, so a run completed with `--gate failed` or `--gate not-run` (the documented surface is `--gate passed|failed|not-run`, `reckon/crew/AGENTS.md:28)`, whose head is by construction unmerged, is refused; the only remedies §5 names are `--land` or merging first, which would put rejected work on main

findings.reason: a node builds controls literally, and a control bound to the wrong arm either measures nothing or is dropped, so the unpushed-head guard would have no negative control in a strict-verification gate.
findings.text: the done-when reads "a reachable remote that carries no primary ref refuses naming the missing ref, with a negative control in which reading that empty answer as promotable promotes it, with a negative control in which reading local HEAD promotes it": the local-HEAD control has been comma-attached to the missing-ref arm, where it does not control that arm, while the arm it actually falsifies ("a head fast-forwarded on local `main` but not pushed") now names no control

findings.reason: the deliverable must keep three causes distinct because the done-when requires each named separately, and the clause as written invites a node to report a missing-ref or fetch-failure cause for the unpushed head.
findings.text: §5's sentence "If the fetch fails, or the helper answers no remote-tracking ref, the complete refuses and names that cause rather than promoting, which a fast-forwarded but unpushed head already satisfies" attaches the unpushed-head case to the fetch-failure/missing-ref causes, but a fast-forwarded local `main` against a reachable remote with a present primary ref produces neither of those causes: the fetch succeeds and the ref exists, so the refusal is the ancestry one
